title: From the Editor — No Names Today
settingText: Rowan Hold as a lived family homestead: work tables, laundry, ledgers, food preparation, shaded yard, and an old black Sunforge rib used as an ordinary piece of the landscape. A goat may stand on it. Warm, human, almost suspiciously normal.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 7. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: After weeks of wrong names, planted stories, borrowed histories, and people insisting Brandon belongs to them, the road offers something almost suspicious.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A town that does not care.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rowan Hold has work to do, supper to make, arguments to finish, and absolutely no interest in turning Brandon Mack into anybody else.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Eva, this is inconvenient.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Brandon, it may be paradise.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For Jessie, it means there is finally room to notice somebody else’s problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No names today.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: Rowan Hold
summary: The trio enters Rowan Hold, a close agricultural settlement where an exposed black rib is used as ordinary seating. Nobody reacts to Brandon as anything but another traveler.

panelPlan.text: Rowan Hold sits around shade trees, low stone houses, garden plots and a communal work yard. A black structural rib crosses the yard and supports laundry at one end; a goat stands on the lower curve.
Brandon, Eva and Jessie enter with the reflexive expectation of being noticed.
People glance at the strangers, then return to a loud family dispute near a ledger table.
Eva watches three separate locals ignore Brandon after learning his name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nobody is looking at him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: They're looking. They just don't care.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I could get used to this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I'm leaving tomorrow.

title: Not About Brandon
summary: The dispute consuming Rowan Hold belongs entirely to Nessa Rowan, whose family has chosen her to inherit a vital record-keeping role she never accepted.

panelPlan.text: Ada Rowan argues with her daughter Nessa beside a table of ledgers while relatives try to continue chores around them.
Nessa has a packed travel bag at her feet, making the argument concrete.
Jessie notices the bag before she understands the job.
Brandon is handed a basket of beans by a child and accidentally becomes useful background to somebody else's story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: They chose you after you made that plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: They chose me because they thought it would stop the plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: What did they choose you for?

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: A life I didn't apply for.

title: Mira's Work
summary: Nessa's aunt Mira kept the Rowan family's births, debts, marriages, property promises and dispute records for twenty-two years. After Mira's death, the family selected Nessa because she already helped with the work.

panelPlan.text: Nessa shows Eva and Jessie a cool interior record room lined with practical handwritten ledgers, boxes and tied bundles.
Ada explains that Mira remembered not just facts but context: who was angry, which debt was forgiven and which promise had conditions.
Nessa demonstrates that she knows the filing system because she helped Mira during busy seasons.
Jessie recognizes competence being used as evidence of consent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Mira trusted her with every name we have.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: She trusted me to help. She did not appoint me from the grave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: How long did Mira do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Twenty-two years.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That number would worry me too.

title: A Job That Becomes a Life
summary: Nessa explains why a temporary compromise does not reassure her. Every relative promises she would serve only until someone else is trained, but nobody can identify that future person or a date when the obligation ends.

panelPlan.text: Nessa stacks the ledgers she would be expected to manage and shows how work arrives every day from multiple households.
She says one uncle offered a year, Ada said until a replacement was trained and another relative simply assumed she would settle into it.
Eva initially suggests a year might be manageable.
Nessa asks Eva to name the replacement who will be ready in a year.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Could you do it for one year and leave after?

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: My uncle said a year. My mother said until someone is trained.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: Nobody has chosen someone to train.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Temporary work without an exit usually stops being temporary.

title: Ada's Problem
summary: Ada's position is also real: Rowan Hold depends on records that prevent old debts and family disputes from becoming permanent feuds. Mira's death created an immediate hole, not merely an unwanted tradition.

panelPlan.text: Ada takes Jessie to a shaded table where two cousins are already arguing over an old boundary agreement.
A ledger entry resolves whether an irrigation ditch was loaned seasonally or transferred permanently.
Ada shows several other current disputes waiting for review.
Jessie acknowledges the work is necessary without agreeing Nessa must perform it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Without the records, every old promise becomes whoever remembers loudest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then the work matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Nessa is the only person ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Those are different facts.

title: Nessa's Problem
summary: Nessa loves the people asking her to stay. That is why the pressure works. Her refusal is not a rejection of Rowan Hold but a refusal to let love become permanent assignment.

panelPlan.text: Nessa helps an elderly relative find an old debt entry with obvious affection and patience.
A child runs in to ask Nessa where a birth record is stored; she answers from memory.
Eva sees why the family believes Nessa is perfect for the role.
Nessa says being able to do the work does not make wanting another life disloyal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I love these people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They can tell.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: That is why everybody thinks loving them should answer the question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It doesn't.

title: Meanwhile, Brandon
summary: Brandon spends the afternoon doing ordinary work while nobody assigns him a past. Eva realizes how unusual the absence of a Brandon-centered event now feels to her.

panelPlan.text: Brandon shells beans with two children and is unexpectedly slow at it.
He helps lift a shade frame using the black rib as an anchor point without commenting on the material.
A local asks his actual name only to know whose cup is whose at supper.
Eva watches him laugh at losing a bean-shelling race and catches herself waiting for a wrong name that never comes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: You are bad at this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I am learning that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nobody here thinks you're somebody else.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Please don't announce it. We might ruin the day.

title: The Packed Bag
summary: Jessie checks Nessa's travel bag and discovers she has packed like someone with determination but no road experience: too many books, too few socks and several useless comforts.

panelPlan.text: Nessa opens her packed bag on a bench for Jessie after asking whether the load is realistic.
Jessie removes three heavy books, a decorative kettle and a second blanket while adding spare socks and repair cord.
Eva watches Jessie become unexpectedly patient and specific.
Nessa asks how Jessie learned to pack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Three books and one spare pair of socks is a philosophy, not a packing plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: The books matter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then choose one and keep your feet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You've inspected the entire bag.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Someone should before the road does.

title: Jessie's First Bag
summary: Jessie admits nobody checked her first travel bag. Her mistakes were tools instead of books, and the memory gives Eva a rare glimpse of Jessie before the road made her competent.

panelPlan.text: Jessie repacks Nessa's gear while Eva asks who taught her.
Jessie says nobody did; she learned by carrying the wrong things until she stopped.
Nessa asks what Jessie overpacked.
Jessie describes hauling duplicate tools because she trusted equipment more than people she might ask for help.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did somebody do this for you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: No. That is how I learned about the socks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: What did you carry too much of?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Tools. I packed like every broken machine was personally waiting for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That sounds more like you than the books.

title: Because I Wanted To
summary: Nessa asks why Jessie first left home. Jessie gives an answer too ordinary to romanticize and too important to dismiss: she wanted to go.

panelPlan.text: The three sit in late shade beside the repacked bag.
Nessa asks whether Jessie left because of a fight, danger or a job.
Jessie says she left because she wanted to see what happened if she did.
Eva recognizes that the lack of a dramatic reason is precisely what gives the choice weight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: Why did you leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Because I wanted to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: That was enough?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: It was enough to get me out the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The rest came afterward.

title: A Fair Solution
summary: The Rowan family proposes what sounds like a democratic solution: vote on who should carry Mira's work. Because Nessa is clearly the most qualified, the vote is functionally a vote on whether she is allowed to leave.

panelPlan.text: Relatives gather in the common yard after supper and propose a formal vote so no one person can be accused of forcing Nessa.
Ada presents the procedure as fairness: every adult household gets a voice.
Nessa asks what happens if the majority chooses her and she still leaves.
The family has no prepared answer because the vote was designed to produce consent rather than encounter refusal.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Nobody wants to force you. We can vote.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: On who carries the records?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: On who the family trusts with the work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: What happens if the answer is me and I still leave?

title: The Vote Begins
summary: The family votes sincerely, and each argument for Nessa reveals how competence, love and reliability can become pressure when everyone treats them as public resources.

panelPlan.text: One relative votes for Nessa because she knows Mira's system. Another because she has the patience to mediate arguments. Another because she is unmarried and presumed more available.
Nessa stands beside the circle rather than within it, arms folded, listening to people describe why her life is convenient for them.
Jessie grows visibly irritated at the unmarried argument.
Brandon watches the physical arrangement before he says anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Relative
dialogueInline.text: Nessa already knows the books.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second Relative
dialogueInline.text: She is good with people who are angry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Third Relative
dialogueInline.text: She has fewer obligations than most of us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: You are describing why my time is useful to you.

title: Outside the Circle
summary: Brandon notices the physical truth before the procedural one: the family has arranged itself in a voting circle while Nessa, whose life is being assigned, stands outside it.

panelPlan.text: A wide panel makes the geometry unmistakable: family members seated in a rough circle, Nessa standing just beyond them beside her packed bag.
Someone asks Brandon whether travelers have a custom for choosing a keeper of records.
Brandon says he has no useful custom, then asks whether Nessa gets a vote.
Ada says Nessa is part of the family and therefore represented by the process.

dialogueInline.speaker: Relative
dialogueInline.text: How do travelers choose who keeps records?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Poorly, in my experience.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Does the person carrying the work get a vote?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: She is family. This vote includes her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: She is standing outside the circle.

title: Consent
summary: The family objects that Brandon is not one of them. He agrees, but points out that a majority can distribute shared work without being able to manufacture one person's consent to a life assignment.

panelPlan.text: Ada tells Brandon the matter belongs to family.
Brandon immediately agrees and starts to step away, refusing the role of outsider-savior.
Before leaving, he distinguishes deciding how records will be kept from deciding that Nessa must keep them.
Jessie backs the distinction without turning the argument into travelers versus locals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: You are not family.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: No, ma'am. This is yours to solve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: But choosing that the records must be kept is not the same as choosing Nessa to keep them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You can divide work. You cannot vote somebody into wanting it.

title: I Love You Anyway
summary: Nessa ends the vote by stating what no procedure can replace: she loves her family and is leaving anyway.

panelPlan.text: Nessa steps into the circle for the first time, not to vote but to speak.
She thanks relatives who trusted her and says she will spend tonight explaining Mira's system as far as she can.
She refuses to let that help become evidence that she has changed her mind.
Ada realizes the family now has to solve the record problem under the assumption Nessa will truly be gone tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I love you. I am leaving anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I will spend tonight teaching anyone who wants to learn the books.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: That is help. It is not an application.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Then we have one night.

title: The Empty Chair
summary: Once Nessa's departure is treated as real, the family stops debating whether she should stay and begins the harder practical work of distributing Mira's responsibilities among willing people.

panelPlan.text: The record room fills with several relatives, each taking a different stack rather than one person inheriting the entire room.
One cousin takes births and marriages, another property agreements, Ada agrees to mediate disputes until a rotation is established.
Nessa explains indexing and where Mira hid corrections to older entries.
The central chair remains empty because no single replacement has been crowned.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: I can take disputes through winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Relative
dialogueInline.text: I can keep births and marriages if somebody checks my handwriting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: Mira's correction book is under the third shelf. She distrusted her own first drafts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The job got smaller when you stopped making one person hold all of it.

title: Packing With Ada
summary: Ada helps Nessa pack. The reconciliation is incomplete: Ada remains hurt and afraid, while still choosing to prepare her daughter for the road rather than sabotage the departure.

panelPlan.text: In Nessa's room, Ada silently folds clothing while Nessa secures the lighter bag Jessie helped arrange.
Ada removes one family ledger Nessa had packed and replaces it with a small recipe book that belongs to her personally.
Nessa asks whether Ada wants her to stay. Ada says wanting is not the same as deciding.
They finish packing without a dramatic embrace, but the bag is no longer a battlefield.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: You still want me to stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Very much.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: That is different from choosing for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: I am learning the difference late.

title: The Road Is Not a Reward
summary: Jessie makes sure Nessa does not treat leaving as proof that every future decision will be right. Freedom includes bad days, loneliness, money problems and the ability to choose again.

panelPlan.text: At dawn, Jessie checks Nessa's straps and water capacity one last time.
Nessa says Jessie makes the road sound miserable.
Jessie lists practical failures without trying to frighten her back into staying.
Eva realizes Jessie is defending choice, not travel as a superior way of life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: You make the road sound miserable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Some days it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: Then why stay out there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Because if I wake up wanting to leave, I can.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The choice matters more than the direction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That is closer.

title: Nessa Leaves
summary: Nessa joins a small caravan taking another road. Her family does not become uniformly supportive; some wave, some remain angry and some immediately return to work.

panelPlan.text: A small trade caravan waits at the far edge of Rowan Hold.
Nessa shoulders the lighter bag and says goodbye to Ada first.
Several relatives wave. One uncle turns back to the record room without waving. The mixed reactions remain visible.
Nessa leaves with the caravan while the trio stays another day rather than making her departure about joining them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ada Rowan
dialogueInline.text: Write when you know where letters can find you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I will.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Check your water before the north cut.

dialogueInline.speaker: Nessa
dialogueInline.text: I kept the socks.

title: A Second Ordinary Day
summary: The trio remains at Rowan Hold long enough to confirm the absence of a Brandon event is not merely delayed. Life continues around him without identity pressure.

panelPlan.text: Brandon spends a second morning helping repair a shade frame and trading labor for food.
Eva checks with three residents whether any traveler recently asked about Brandon or another identity; nobody did.
The goat again occupies the black rib, indifferent to Eva's notebook.
Jessie tells Eva that nothing happening is allowed to be the result.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: No preacher. No wrong name. No person waiting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then write that down and stop trying to improve it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The goat spent most of yesterday on the Sunforge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The goat is not helping your case.

title: Brandon, Entirely
summary: As they prepare to leave, Eva acknowledges that Rowan Hold learned Brandon only as Brandon and found nothing remarkable about the fact. Brandon values the experience more than she does.

panelPlan.text: A child returns Brandon's knife after using it for supper preparation, addressing him correctly without ceremony.
Ada thanks Jessie for helping Nessa pack, still with mixed feelings.
Eva closes a notebook page containing mostly crossed-out expectations.
Brandon receives a wrapped piece of bread from a local who never asked about his past.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Two days and you were Brandon the entire time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It was an excellent two days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You also lost to a child at bean shelling.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I had an excellent supper afterward.

title: No Names Today
summary: The trio leaves Rowan Hold with a useful negative case: Brandon, a conspicuous Sunforge remnant and a socially distinct community can coexist without the identity pattern appearing at all.

panelPlan.text: The rig pulls away while Rowan Hold returns to ordinary work.
Eva looks back at the black rib and closes the theory page rather than forcing a connection.
Jessie says the place does not disprove every correlation, but it prevents them from treating one as automatic.
Far ahead, the road begins opening toward the broad pale terrain of the Long Mile.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The Sunforge was there. Brandon was there. Nothing happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That belongs in the notebook too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Please make 'nothing happened' our new specialty.

title: Next: THE FARTHER RIDER
settingText: A vast pale ridge on the Long Mile with one tiny rider silhouette against the sky. The foreground road is empty. The figure is distant enough to dismiss and visually difficult to stop looking at.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 7. Point directly at the next loaded pressure without revealing its resolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Two whole days.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No wrong name.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No waiting enemy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No conspiracy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No mystery.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the road opens onto the Long Mile.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is someone on the ridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Far enough away to ignore.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Close enough to keep seeing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: THE FARTHER RIDER
